

# 

# 1\. Safety Rules

**S01 Be Safe.** Team members may not behave in a way that risks injury to themselves or others. This applies to everywhere in the camp, not only at the field. *Violation: Verbal Warning. Yellow Card or Red Cards for repeat or egregious violations.*

**S02 Stay out of the field.** No person may enter the field or reach past the field boundary while a Match is in progress. *Violation: Major Penalty. Red card if the action affects the Match outcome or creates a safety risk.*

**S03 A referee may stop a robot.** A referee may declare a Robot Disabled at any time for safety or for field damage. A Disabled Robot must stop all motion immediately and scores nothing for the remainder of the Match. *Violation: Red Card.*

# 2\. Game Overview

*Are you ready to revolutionize the field? In **Iron Acres** you engineer and pilot a custom robot to tackle an agricultural challenge. Robots dump Silos in a fast autonomous sprint, gather Crops from the field, and deliver them to the Factory. Human Players convert Crops into Products, and Robots haul those Products to the City. In the final seconds, Robots race back to the Barn to park or hang.*

*Two Alliances of two Teams each compete in a Match. The Alliance with more points wins.*  
![][image1]

# 3	The Arena

---

# 3.1 The Field

![][image2]  
The field is 108 in. (274.32 cm) long by 54 in. (137.16 cm) wide.

The Center Line is a 1 in. wide grey line spanning the 54 in. width of the field, located 54 in. from each short wall. It divides the field into two halves.

# 3.2 Zones

Each Alliance has the following zones. All are marked with alliance-colored tape.

**Factory.** A 12 in. (30.48 cm) square marked by alliance-colored tape. Robots deliver Crops here.

**Factory Zone.** The Factory plus the adjacent area outside the field where the Human Player stands and where the Factory Storage Container sits.

**City.** The area enclosed by the City boundary wall, measured to the inside face of the wall. The boundary wall is 2 in. (5.08 cm) tall and 12 in. by 12 in. measured to its outside faces.

**City Perimeter.** The area between the outside face of the City boundary wall and the outside edge of the City Perimeter tape, plus the tape itself. The tape is placed 2 in. (5.08 cm) from the City boundary wall.

**Protected Zone.** The City and the City Perimeter together. Opponent Robots may not enter or contact Robots inside an Alliance's Protected Zone. See G07 and G13.

**Barn.** An alliance-colored taped area 9 in. (22.86 cm) by 22.4 in. (56.896 cm). Robots start the Match here and may Park or Hang here at the end. Each Barn has one Barn Bar.

# 3.3 Field Elements

**Barn Bar.** A horizontal bar 25.236 in. (641 mm) wide spanning the Barn.

* Underside of the bar: 4.00 in. (101.6 mm) above the field floor.  
* Top of the bar: 5.05 in. (128.3 mm) above the field floor.

![][image3]  
**Silo Holder.** A structure built from XBS components, 7.3 in. (185.4 mm) high by 7.795 in. (198 mm) wide. Its front plate is designed so that pushing it tips the Silo, dumping the Crops.  
 ![][image4]

**Silo.** A deli-style tub that rests upright on top of a Silo Holder. Nominal dimensions are 4.173 in. (106 mm) diameter by 5.906 in. (150 mm) tall. Tubs need not match exactly, but must rest stably on the Silo Holder and hold at least 10 Crops.  
![][image5]  
**Factory Storage Container.** A container outside the field, in the Factory Zone, into which the Human Player places Crops to release Products. An extra Silo tub works. Contents are counted after the Match.  
**3.4 Game Pieces** 

**Crop.** A wiffle golf ball 40 mm to 43 mm in diameter. There are 40 Crops on the field, shared between both Alliances.

**Product.** A rectangular 3D-printed object measuring 1.5 in. (38.1 mm) by 2.5 in. (63.5 mm).  
![][image6]

**3.5 Field Setup**

**Crops.** Up to 40 Crops start inside the Silos, evenly distributed per Silo. Teams may pre-load up to 4 crops each. Crops not pre-loaded are loaded into the silos.

**Products.** 12 Products per Team, in that Team's Human Player area. None on the field.

**Robots.** Wheels inside their Alliance's Barn. See G01.

# 4	**Match Play**

---

**4.1 Match Structure**

| Period | Duration |
| :---- | :---- |
| Autonomous | 0:10 |
| Driver-Controlled | 2:30 |
| Endgame | Final 0:30 of Driver-Controlled |
| **Total** | **2:40** |

A sound signals the start of Autonomous, the start of Driver-Controlled, the start of Endgame, and the end of the Match.

Endgame is a signal to Drive Teams, not a separate scoring window. Parking and Hanging are evaluated at the end of the Match regardless of when a Robot arrives.

**4.2 Match Setup**

Teams place Robots in their starting positions and may Preload Crops. Do not step on field elements while placing a Robot.

**4.3 Autonomous Period**

At the start of Autonomous, each driver may press one button or key one time to signal their Robot. After that, Drive Teams may not touch their controls until the Driver-Controlled Period begins. See G02.

**4.4 Driver Controlled Period**

Drivers control their Robots freely. When the Match ends, drivers must stop providing input immediately.

# 5	**Scoring**

---

**5.1  Scoring Definitions**

These definitions determine what counts. A referee applies them at the end of the Match unless a definition states otherwise.

**Crop Scored.** A Crop is Scored if, at the end of the Match, it is Completely Inside the Factory or is inside the Factory Storage Container. A Crop that has been Scored and later removed from both locations is not Scored.

**Product Scored in the City Center.** A Product is Scored in the City Center if, at the end of the Match, it is Completely Inside the City and is not Possessed by a Robot.

**Product Scored in the City Limits.** A Product is Scored in the City Limits if, at the end of the Match, it is at least partially Inside the City Perimeter, is not Completely Inside the City, and is not Possessed by a Robot.

* A Product is never Scored in both locations. It earns the higher value only.  
* A Product resting on top of the City boundary wall is Scored in the City Limits, not the City Center. A Product resting on another Product is Scored normally by its own position.

**Silo Dumped.** A Silo is Dumped when its tub is no longer resting upright on its Silo Holder. A Silo counts only during the Autonomous Period, counts once, and is credited to the Alliance whose Robot caused it to tip.

**Parked.** A Robot is Parked if, at the end of the Scoring Period, it is at least partially Inside its alliance’s Scoring Regions’ tape.

**Hanging.** A Robot is Hanging if, at the end of the Match, it is supported solely by a Barn Bar and is not in contact with the Barn uprights, another Robot, or any other field element.

* A Robot that is Hanging is not also Parked. More than one Robot may Hang from the same Barn Bar, and each earns points.

**5.2  Points Values**

| Autonomous | Points Earned |
| :---- | :---: |
| *Parking*  in the *Factory*  | 5 |
| *Crops* scored in the *Factory* | 7 |
| *Silo* dumped  | 5 |
| **Driver controlled** |  |
| *Crops* scored in the *Factory* | 7 |
| *Products* in the City Limits | 10 |
| *Products* in the City Center | 15 |
| **Endgame** |  |
| Parking in the barn | 5 |
| Hanging from the *Barn* | 25 |

# 6	**Game Rules**

---

**G01 Starting configuration.** At the start of a Match, each Robot must be in its Alliance's Barn with all of its wheels Completely Inside the Barn tape, and must not be in contact with another Robot. A Robot may Preload up to 4 Crops and may not Preload a Product. *Violation: The Robot may not participate in the Autonomous Period. If discovered after the Match starts, Minor Penalty.*

**G02 Hands off during Autonomous.** After the single permitted button press, no Drive Team member may touch or interact with their Robot or their controls until the Driver-Controlled Period begins. *Violation: Minor Penalty, and the offending Robot scores no Autonomous points. Yellow Card for repeat violations. This penalty affects only the offending Team, not their Alliance partner.*

**G03 Stay on your half during Autonomous.** During the Autonomous Period, no part of a Robot may cross the Center Line. *Violation: Minor Penalty. Yellow Card if repeated or strategic.*

**G04 Two Products maximum.** A Robot may Possess no more than two Products at a time. *Violation: Minor Penalty per Product over the limit, plus an additional Minor Penalty per Product for each 5 seconds the condition continues.*

**G05 No launching or throwing.** No Robot and no team member may launch, throw, or otherwise propel a game piece through the air. Rolling a Crop along the field floor is permitted. *Violation: Major Penalty per game piece. Throwing a game piece at a person is an automatic Red Card.*

**G06 No pinning.** A Robot may not Pin an opponent Robot for more than 3 seconds. Pinning is holding an opponent Robot against a field element so that it cannot escape. The pinning Robot must retreat at least 6 in. (15.24 cm) to clear the count. *Violation: Minor Penalty per 3 second interval.*

**G07 Stay out of the opponent's Protected Zone.** A Robot may not contact an opponent Robot that is Inside its own Alliance's Protected Zone. *Violation: Major Penalty per occurrence.*

**G08 No descoring your opponent.** A Robot may not remove a Crop or Product from the opposing Alliance's Factory, City, or City Perimeter. *Violation: Minor Penalty per game piece. Red Card if repeated or strategic.*

**G09 No damage.** A Robot may not damage or functionally impair another Robot or the field. *Violation: Minor Penalty if incidental. Major Penalty escalating to a Red Card if deliberate.*

**G10 Keep your parts.** A Robot may not intentionally detach parts or leave parts on the field. *Violation: Major Penalty per Match.*

**G11 Stay on the field.** A Robot may not leave the field or climb on the field boundary. *Violation: Minor Penalty. The Robot is Disabled for the remainder of the Match if it cannot return under its own power.*

**G12 Game pieces out of play.** A game piece that leaves the field is out of play for the remainder of the Match and scores nothing. Field staff return it during field reset, not during the Match.

**G13 Do not block scoring in the Protected Zone.** A Robot may not prevent an opponent from Scoring a Product in the opponent's own City or City Perimeter. *Violation: Major Penalty per occurrence.*

**G14 Do not interfere with another team's control link.** No team may take any action that disrupts another team's wireless connection to their Robot. This includes operating a Robot's radio outside a Match in a way that interferes with a Match in progress. *Violation: Major Penalty. Red Card if deliberate.*

**G15 Egregious behavior.** Behavior beyond what is listed in these rules, or repeated violation of any rule, is prohibited. The Head Referee may assign a Yellow Card or Red Card for egregious Robot actions or team member behavior anywhere at the event. *Violation: Yellow Card or Red Card.*

# 7	**Human Player and Drive Team Rules**

---

**H01 Drive Team composition.** A Drive Team consists of 1 driver, 1 Human Player, and 1 optional coach per Team. Drive Team members remain in their Alliance's designated area for the whole Match. *Violation: Verbal Warning. Minor Penalty for repeat violations.*

**H02 Your Factory Zone only.** A Human Player may interact with game pieces only within their own Alliance's Factory Zone. *Violation: Minor Penalty per occurrence.*

**H03 Four Crops per Product.** A Human Player may release one Product for every four Crops they have placed into their Factory Storage Container. Crops in the Container may not be removed. *Violation: Minor Penalty per Product released without backing Crops, and that Product does not Score.*

**H04 Place, do not adjust.** A Human Player may place a Product onto a Robot. Once the Product is in contact with the Robot, the Human Player may not touch, adjust, or reposition it. A Human Player may not touch any Crop or Product that is already in contact with a Robot. *Violation: Minor Penalty per occurrence.*

**H05 Reach responsibly.** A Human Player reaching into their own Factory may not use their hands, arms, or body to block, deflect, guide, or shield a Robot or a game piece in motion. Reaching is permitted for handling game pieces and for placing a Product under H04, and for nothing else. *Violation: Minor Penalty per occurrence. Major Penalty if it affects Scoring or Robot motion.*

**H06 Show up.** A Team must send at least one Drive Team member to every scheduled Match, whether or not their Robot is available. *Violation: The Team is recorded as a no-show and scores 0 for that Match. Their Alliance partner's score is unaffected.*

# 8	**Robot Construction Rules**

---

Every Robot must pass Inspection before its first Match. A Robot that is modified after Inspection must be re-inspected before its next Match. See the checklist in Appendix A.

**R01 Size.** A Robot may not extend beyond a 10 in. (25.4 cm) cube at any time, in any configuration, during a Match. Inspection is performed using the event sizing box. *Violation: Robot fails Inspection. If discovered during a Match, Major Penalty and the Robot is Disabled.*

**R02 Platform.** A Robot must be built on an XRP chassis using an XRP Controller as its sole control system. *Violation: Robot fails Inspection.*

**R03 No field-damaging materials.** A Robot may not use adhesives that contact the field, exposed sharp or abrasive edges, or wheels and traction devices that mark or cut the field surface. *Violation: Robot fails Inspection.*

**R04 Team marker.** A Robot must display a 2 in. by 2 in. team marker showing its assigned Team number, mounted in the groove of the XRP chassis, secure enough that it cannot fall out during a Match. Each Team must have both a red and a blue marker and must display the one matching their Alliance. *Violation: Robot fails Inspection. If discovered during a Match, Verbal Warning, then Minor Penalty for repeat occurrences.*

**R05 Control.** A Robot may respond only to its own Drive Team's control device. Robots must use the wireless configuration assigned at the competition. *Violation: Robot fails Inspection. See also G14.*

**R06 Power.** A Robot may be powered only by 4 AA batteries. Batteries must be secured so that they cannot fall out during a Match. *Violation: Robot fails Inspection.*

**R07 Facilitator additions.** A facilitator may add Robot rules in the areas of safety or permitted materials. A facilitator will not change Robot size, platform, or control system requirements.

# 9       Tournament Rules

---

**T01 Schedule.** The competition consists of 2 versus 2 Matches. Every Team plays the same number of Matches.

**T02 Scoring.** Each Team receives the full score of their Alliance in each Match, including penalty points awarded to their Alliance.

**T03 Penalties.** A Penalty awards points to the non-offending Alliance.

| Tier | Points |
| :---- | :---- |
| Minor Penalty | 10 |
| Major Penalty | 25 |

Penalties are assessed per occurrence unless the rule states otherwise. Penalty points are added to the non-offending Alliance's score and count toward both of that Alliance's Teams.

**T04 Yellow and Red Cards.**

A Yellow Card is a formal warning. It carries no point value. A Team that has received a Yellow Card carries it forward for the remainder of the tournament.

Yellow Cards are additive. A second Yellow Card to the same Team is automatically converted to a Red Card.

A Red Card results in a score of 0 for that Team in that Match.

Cards are issued by the Head Referee and announced after the Match, with the violation stated aloud.

**T05 Disqualification.** A Team that receives three Red Cards is disqualified from the event. Their scheduled Matches continue with their partner playing alone.

**T06 Match replay.** A Match is replayed only if a field fault, a timer failure, or a referee error materially affected the outcome. The Head Referee decides. No video, photo, or recording from any source is reviewed.

**T07 Rule interpretation.** Each event has one Head Referee. Their rulings are final for that event.

# 11	Glossary

---

**Alliance.** Two Teams playing together in a Match, designated red or blue.

**Autonomous Period.** The first 10 seconds of a Match, during which Robots operate without driver input.

**Completely Inside.** An object entirely within the upward vertical extension of an area's boundary. The boundary element (tape, wall, marking) is part of the area.

**Disabled.** A Robot that is no longer active for the remainder of a Match, due to failure or by order of a referee.

**Endgame.** The final 30 seconds of the Driver-Controlled Period. A signal to Drive Teams, not a separate scoring window.

**Human Player.** A student Team member who handles game pieces in the Factory Zone.

**Inside.** An object that has crossed into the upward vertical extension of an area's boundary. Compare Completely Inside.

**Inspection.** The check that a Robot meets Section 8 before it competes.

**Major Penalty.** 25 points to the non-offending Alliance.

**Match.** One 2 minute 45 second contest between two Alliances.

**Minor Penalty.** 10 points to the non-offending Alliance.

**Pin.** Holding an opponent Robot against a field element so it cannot escape. See G07.

**Possess.** An object is Possessed by a Robot if, as the Robot moves or changes orientation, the object stays in approximately the same position relative to the Robot. Carrying and holding are Possession. Bumping a Crop while driving is not.

**Preload.** A game piece placed on or in a Robot during Match setup.

**Team.** One group of students with one Robot and one assigned number.

**Verbal Warning.** A spoken caution from the Head Referee. Carries no points. Persists for the event.
